Define the conditional entropy in nats by

$$H(X|Y):=\sum_{y:p_Y(y)>0}p_Y(y)H(p_{X|y}),$$

For each $v$ with $p_V(v)>0$, the conditional vector $p_{U|v}(u):=p_{UV}(u,v)/p_V(v)$ is a probability vector; likewise for conditioning on positive-mass $u$. Consequently, if $p_{UVW}$ is a finite joint pmf, then for every $w$ with $p_W(w)>0$, $p_{UV|w}$ and its two marginals are probability vectors.

For a finite nonempty set identified with $[k]=\{1,\ldots,k\}$, a **probability vector** is $p=(p_i)_{i=1}^k$ with $p_i\ge0$ and $\sum_i p_i=1$; it is the outcome-weight vector of a finite probability space ([[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]). Its Shannon entropy in natural units is
$$H(p):=-\sum_{i=1}^k p_i\ln p_i,$$
with $0\ln0:=0$. For probability vectors $p,q$ on the same set $[k]$, the relative entropy is
$$D(p\|q):=\sum_{i:p_i>0}p_i\ln(p_i/q_i),$$
with value $+\infty$ if $p_i>0=q_i$ for some $i$. A matrix $A\in[0,1]^{N\times m}$ is **row-stochastic** when each row sums to one. For each nonempty $S\subseteq[k]$ and supported pair $(x_S^n,x_{S^c}^n)$, define the conditional block information
$$J_{S,n}(x_S^n\mid x_{S^c}^n):=-\frac1n\ln P^{\otimes n}(x_S^n\mid x_{S^c}^n),$$
where the conditional probability is the finite conditional law of the block under $P^{\otimes n}$. Its positive denominator and coordinatewise factorization on supported tuples are proved in [[lem-it-multisource-block-conditional-law-factorization]].

For $\delta,\epsilon>0$, the **jointly typical set** is
$$\mathcal T_n(P,\delta,\epsilon):=\left\{z^n\in\mathcal X_+^n:\|\widehat P_{z^n}-P\|_\infty\le\delta,\ |I_n(z^n)-H(P)|\le\epsilon,\ |J_{S,n}(x_S^n\mid x_{S^c}^n)-H_P(X_S\mid X_{S^c})|\le\epsilon\text{ for every nonempty }S\subseteq[k]\right\}.$$

Let $\mathcal A$ be a finite nonempty alphabet and let $n\ge1$. A word of length $n$ is $x^n=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\mathcal A^n$. For $a\in\mathcal A$, define its count and empirical type by
$$N(a\mid x^n):=\#\{i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}:x_i=a\},\qquad \widehat P_{x^n}(a):=\frac{N(a\mid x^n)}n.$$
Every position contributes to exactly one count, so the coordinates of $\widehat P_{x^n}$ are nonnegative and sum to one; it is a probability vector in the sense of [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]]. The **set of $n$-types** is $\mathcal P_n(\mathcal A):=\{\widehat P_{x^n}:x^n\in\mathcal A^n\}$. The map $x^n\mapsto\widehat P_{x^n}$ has these type classes as its fibers.

$$f_{i,n}:\mathcal X_i^n\to[M_i]:=\{1,\ldots,M_i\},\qquad 1\le i\le k,$$

$$g_n:\prod_{i=1}^k[M_i]\to\prod_{i=1}^k\mathcal X_i^n.$$
Its block-error probability is
$$P_e^{(n)}:=\mathbb P\!\left[g_n\bigl(f_{1,n}(X_1^n),\ldots,f_{k,n}(X_k^n)\bigr)\ne(X_1^n,\ldots,X_k^n)\right].$$

A vector $R=(R_1,\ldots,R_k)\in[0,\infty)^k$ is **achievable** if there are strictly increasing blocklengths $n_j\to\infty$ and such codes for which $P_e^{(n_j)}\to0$ and $\limsup_{j\to\infty}R_{i,n_j}\le R_i$ for every $i$. By [F2], along the achieving blocklengths and for all sufficiently large $n$, the product message count $M_S:=\prod_{i\in S}M_i$ obeys $n^{-1}\ln M_S\le R_S+\gamma/4$, since each of the finitely many coordinate rate limsups is at most $R_i$.

Fix such a blocklength and a complement word $x_{S^c}^n$ of positive probability. Its complement message indices are then fixed. For each possible $S$-message tuple, the common decoder outputs at most one candidate $x_S^n$, so at most $M_S$ values of $x_S^n$ can be decoded correctly for this complement word.

For achievability, take any $R\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SW}}(P)$ and any slack $a>0$. Put $\rho_i:=R_i+a$ and $\eta:=a/2$. Then for every nonempty $S$, $\sum_{i\in S}\rho_i\ge H_S+|S|a\ge H_S+a$. For this $n$, set $M_i:=\lceil e^{n\rho_i}\rceil$. For every encoder $i$, independently assign each word in $\mathcal X_i^n$ a uniform label in $[M_i]$, with all word-label assignments independent across words and encoders. The decoder returns the unique jointly typical source tuple having the received vector of labels; if there is not exactly one, it returns a fixed default tuple from fixed finite listings of the nonempty alphabets. Therefore the probability that all message labels of the competitor equal the true labels is $\prod_{i\in S}M_i^{-1}$.

Choose the typical set $\mathcal T_n(P,1,\gamma/4)$. For any supported block in this set, [F3] gives $P^{\otimes n}(x_S^n\mid x_{S^c}^n)\le e^{-n(H_S-\gamma/4)}$. If the true tuple is typical, decoding error requires at least one distinct typical competitor to share its message vector. Indeed, $M_i\ge e^{n(R_i+a)}$ and $\sum_{i\in S}(R_i+a)\ge H_S+|S|a$, leaving exponent at most $-a/2$ for each $S$.

By [F4], $P(Z^n\notin\mathcal T_n(P,1,\gamma/4))\to0$. Step 2.1 therefore implies the probability of correct decoding tends to zero, so the block-error probability tends to one. This contradicts [F2]. Thus every achievable $R$ satisfies $R_S\ge H_S$ for every nonempty $S$.

The first term in step 2.2 tends to zero by [F4]. For the second, [F6] and $1/t\le1/\sqrt t$ for $t\ge1$ give $\ln(n+1)\le2(\sqrt{n+1}-1)$, hence $m\ln(n+1)/n\to0$ and $(n+1)^me^{-na/2}\to0$. Thus for every fixed $a>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$, there is a deterministic code with error tending to zero and rates $\frac1n\ln M_i\le R_i+a+\frac{\ln2}{n}$, using $\lceil x\rceil\le2x$ for $x\ge1$.

Finally take $a_j:=1/j$ and choose recursively increasing $n_j$ large enough that the selected code's error is at most $1/j$ and $(\ln2)/n_j\le1/j$. Step 3.2 then gives coordinate rate limsups at most $R_i$. These codes make $R$ achievable, including boundary points where one or more subset inequalities are equalities.

$$H(X|Y):=\sum_{y:p_Y(y)>0}p_Y(y)H(p_{X|y}),$$

where $H(p)=-\sum_xp(x)\ln p(x)$ is the finite entropy of [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]]. Terms for zero-mass $y$ are omitted. The base-$b$ version replaces $\ln$ by $\log_b$.

Let $(Z_t)_{t\ge1}$ be a finite-alphabet IID $k$-source with joint law $P$ as in [[def-it-finite-iid-multisource]], where $k\ge2$. The achievable fixed-length lossless rate vectors in the sense of [[def-it-multiterminal-lossless-code]] are exactly
$$\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SW}}(P)=\left\{R\in[0,\infty)^k:\sum_{i\in S}R_i\ge H_P(X_S\mid X_{S^c})\text{ for every nonempty }S\subseteq[k]\right\}.$$
For $S=[k]$, the inequality is the total-rate bound $\sum_iR_i\ge H(P)$. All logarithms are natural, so rates and entropies are in nats per source symbol.

Let $(X,Y)$ have a joint probability vector $p_{XY}$ on finite nonempty alphabets $\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y$. Its **support bipartite graph** has left vertices $x$ with $p_X(x)>0$, right vertices $y$ with $p_Y(y)>0$, and an edge $x\!\text{--}\!y$ exactly when $p_{XY}(x,y)>0$. Let $\mathcal K$ be the finite nonempty set of connected components. Define $K_X(x)$ and $K_Y(y)$ to be the component containing the corresponding vertex when that vertex has positive marginal mass; assign any fixed component label to zero-mass symbols, which do not affect the law of the random labels. Along every support edge the two labels agree, so define the finite random variable $K:=K_X(X)=K_Y(Y)$ almost surely. If $f(X)=g(Y)$ almost surely for any other finite-valued deterministic common output, then $f(x)=g(y)$ along every support edge; equality propagates along graph paths, so both functions are constant on each component and the common output is a function of $K$. Thus $K$ is the maximal deterministic common part up to relabeling. Its finite entropy $H(K)$ is the deterministic Gács–Körner common information, using [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]].

A finite auxiliary random variable $U$ is **Wyner-admissible** for $p_{XY}$ when a joint law $p_{XYU}$ has $(X,Y)$-marginal $p_{XY}$ and, for every $u$ with $p_U(u)>0$,
$$p_{XY\mid U=u}(x,y)=p_{X\mid U=u}(x)p_{Y\mid U=u}(y).$$
The finite-alphabet **Wyner common information** is
$$C_W(X;Y):=\inf_{U\text{ finite, Wyner-admissible}} I((X,Y);U),$$
where mutual information and natural-log units are as in [[def-it-finite-mutual-information]] and [[def-it-information-units-and-logarithm-base]]. The Gács–Körner object is a deterministic common output of both terminals; Wyner's quantity optimizes mutual information over an auxiliary variable that makes the terminals conditionally independent. They are distinct definitions. This page does not identify them or use either as a Slepian–Wolf rate coordinate.

The admissible class is nonempty: $U=(X,Y)$ is finite and makes each positive-mass conditional joint law a product of point masses. Hence the infimum is over a nonempty set of finite real mutual informations.

For a finite nonempty set identified with $[k]=\{1,\ldots,k\}$, a **probability vector** is $p=(p_i)_{i=1}^k$ with $p_i\ge0$ and $\sum_i p_i=1$; it is the outcome-weight vector of a finite probability space ([[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]). Its Shannon entropy in natural units is
$$H(p):=-\sum_{i=1}^k p_i\ln p_i,$$
with $0\ln0:=0$. For probability vectors $p,q$ on the same set $[k]$, the relative entropy is
$$D(p\|q):=\sum_{i:p_i>0}p_i\ln(p_i/q_i),$$
with value $+\infty$ if $p_i>0=q_i$ for some $i$. A matrix $A\in[0,1]^{N\times m}$ is **row-stochastic** when each row sums to one. For a probability row vector $p$ on $[m]$ and a row vector $X\in[0,1]^m$, the dot product $pX^{\mathsf T}=\sum_{i=1}^m p_iX_i$ is the acceptance probability under distribution $p$.

These definitions use finite sets only; entropy is between $0$ and $\ln k$, as proved where needed below.
For finite probability vectors $p,q$ on the same alphabet, $D(p\|q)\ge0$, and $D(p\|q)=0$ if and only if $p=q$. If $p_i>0=q_i$ for some coordinate, then $D(p\|q)=+\infty$.

The function $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and strictly increasing, is onto $\mathbb R$, and satisfies, for $x,y>0$,
$$\log(xy)=\log x+\log y,\qquad \log(x/y)=\log x-\log y,\qquad \log(1/x)=-\log x.$$
Also $\log 1=0$.

Fix an integer $k\ge2$ and finite nonempty alphabets $\mathcal X_1,\ldots,\mathcal X_k$. Let $\mathcal X:=\prod_{i=1}^k\mathcal X_i$, identified with a finite alphabet as in [[def-finite-alphabet-iid-source]]. A **finite-alphabet IID $k$-source** is an IID sequence of vectors
$$Z_t=(X_{1,t},\ldots,X_{k,t})\in\mathcal X,\qquad t\ge1,$$
with common joint probability vector $P$ on $\mathcal X$. Thus for every $n\ge1$ its block law is $P^{\otimes n}$, and terminal $i$ observes $X_i^n=(X_{i,1},\ldots,X_{i,n})$. For $S\subseteq[k]:=\{1,\ldots,k\}$ write $X_S=(X_i)_{i\in S}$, let $S^c=[k]\setminus S$, and define $H_P(X_S\mid X_{S^c})$ by [[def-it-finite-conditional-entropy]] for the induced finite joint law. When $S=[k]$, $X_{S^c}$ takes values in the singleton empty product, so $H_P(X_S\mid X_{S^c})=H(P)$ under [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]]. Unmarked logarithms and information rates use nats by [[def-it-information-units-and-logarithm-base]].

Fix a finite-alphabet IID multisource from [[def-it-finite-iid-multisource]] and a blocklength $n\ge1$. Choose positive integers $M_1,\ldots,M_k$. A **fixed-length multiterminal lossless code** consists of separate deterministic encoders
$$f_{i,n}:\mathcal X_i^n\to[M_i]:=\{1,\ldots,M_i\},\qquad 1\le i\le k,$$
and one common deterministic decoder
$$g_n:\prod_{i=1}^k[M_i]\to\prod_{i=1}^k\mathcal X_i^n.$$
Its block-error probability is
$$P_e^{(n)}:=\mathbb P\!\left[g_n\bigl(f_{1,n}(X_1^n),\ldots,f_{k,n}(X_k^n)\bigr)\ne(X_1^n,\ldots,X_k^n)\right].$$
The rate of encoder $i$ is $R_{i,n}:=n^{-1}\ln M_i$ nats per source symbol, with the logarithm convention of [[def-it-information-units-and-logarithm-base]]. A vector $R=(R_1,\ldots,R_k)\in[0,\infty)^k$ is **achievable** if there are strictly increasing blocklengths $n_j\to\infty$ and such codes for which $P_e^{(n_j)}\to0$ and $\limsup_{j\to\infty}R_{i,n_j}\le R_i$ for every $i$. The encoders do not observe other terminals' source blocks; only the common decoder receives all message indices.
The random-coding construction in steps 1.4–1.5 assigns uniform labels independently across distinct source words and across encoders; its product collision bound uses both independence properties.

derivations.claim: Under [F1], each of the pairs $(0,0)$ and $(1,1)$ has source probability $1/4$. Under independent maps $F_X,F_Y:\{0,1\}\to[M]$, each equality $F_X(0)=F_X(1)$ and $F_Y(0)=F_Y(1)$ has probability $1/M$, because the two labels in each map are independent and uniform. The two equalities are independent across encoders, so both competing pairs collide in both message coordinates with probability $M^{-2}$.

Under a shared map $F_X=F_Y=F$, both message-coordinate collision conditions are the same event $F(0)=F(1)$. Its probability is $1/M$, not $1/M^2$. At $M=2$, the two probabilities are $1/4$ and $1/2$.

The calculation identifies why the independent-map hypothesis in [F3] permits multiplication of per-encoder collision probabilities. It does not claim that every shared-map code is poor; it shows that this particular product bound cannot be used for the shared ensemble.
